title: Rafi's Sorting Fun
markdown:
The sun burst through Rafi’s window. Boing. Rafi popped awake. Today felt special. He bounced out of bed, eager. Outside, dewdrops sparkled. Birds chirped a happy tune.

Downstairs, Plum the rabbit hopped. “Morning, Rafi! Perfect morning for fun!” Mr Reed the badger ambled in. “A splendid morning for clever fun,” he rumbled.

Rafi zoomed over. “Mr Reed! Plum! My toy box is packed with boats. They’re a colourful mess. How can we put them away so they look neat?”

Plum’s ears flopped. “Jumbled boats don’t sound tidy.” Mr Reed chuckled. “A fine puzzle. Let’s put our thinking caps on.”

Rafi picked up a small red boat. “This one’s small.” Then he held up a big blue boat. “And this one is big!”

Plum tried lining them up. “This one, then this one…” The line was still a jumble. “Tricky-tricky!” Plum mumbled.

Rafi watched. Then he picked up a tiny yellow boat. Next, a green one, just a bit bigger. After that, a purple boat, bigger still. Suddenly Rafi’s eyes sparkled. “Wait! Look! This yellow boat is the smallest. And this green one? A bit bigger. And this purple one? Even bigger!”

Mr Reed leaned in. “What do you see, my dear child?”

“They are different sizes!” Rafi beamed. “And we have boxes. A tiny box, a medium box, and a big box. We can put the smallest boats in the smallest box. Then the next smallest boats in the next box. The biggest boats in the biggest box.”

Plum’s ears shot up. “Smallest in the smallest? Biggest in the biggest?”

“Exactly. We sort them. From smallest to biggest.” He grabbed the tiny box. “This little yellow boat fits here.” He picked up a slightly larger blue boat. “And this one goes in this bigger box.” They found three boxes: tiny, medium, and grand.

Rafi and Plum tumbled through the boxes. “This boat is smaller than that one!” chirped Plum, popping it into the correct box. Mr Reed helped guide the bigger boats. They worked together, putting each boat into its perfectly sized home. Soon the boats were lined up, from tiny skiffs to grand galleons. It looked like a beautiful rainbow.

“Wowee!” said Plum, tail thumping. “They fit so perfectly!”

Rafi grinned. “When we put things in order, from smallest to biggest, it keeps everything tidy. It’s like building a perfect line.”

Mr Reed nodded. “Sorting by size is a fantastic way to organise. It makes finding things so much easier.”

Plum bounced. “A super-duper sorting game. And now his boats are all ready for their next big journey.”

“And today,” Rafi declared, grin wide, “is going to be amazing!” With a determined grin, Rafi bounded towards the door, ready for whatever wonderful adventures the amazing day would bring.
characters: Rafi (a question asker), Plum (a rabbit), Reed (a badger)
